title: Waveform, sample rate and spectrograms: ComfyUI's AUDIO type

questions.q: What two things make up an AUDIO value?
options: A waveform tensor [batch, channels, samples] and a sample rate
A tensor [samples, channels, batch] and a file name
Left and right tensors with no rate
questions.answer: A waveform tensor [batch, channels, samples] and a sample rate

questions.q: 88,200 samples at 32000 Hz last how long?
questions.why: Duration is samples / rate. The same tensor lasts 2 s at 44100 Hz. That is why the rate has to travel with it.

questions.q: You raise a 0.5 peak sine by 12 dB with AudioAdjustVolume. What's the peak?
options: About 1.99, because the node has no limiter
questions.answer: About 1.99, because the node has no limiter
questions.why: Gain is 10 ** (12 / 20) = 3.98, and the node just multiplies.

questions.q: You join H3 audio and Music 3 audio with AudioConcat. What rate comes out?
options: 44100 Hz, the higher rate, after the lower one is resampled up
questions.answer: 44100 Hz, the higher rate, after the lower one is resampled up
questions.why: match_audio_sample_rates resamples whichever rate is lower. Upsampling can't restore what a 32000 Hz file never held.

questions.q: Why does a short window smear notes together in a spectrogram?
options: Its bins are wide: at 16 kHz a 128-sample window has 125 Hz per bin
questions.answer: Its bins are wide: at 16 kHz a 128-sample window has 125 Hz per bin
questions.why: Bin width is sample rate / window length. Long windows have narrow bins and smear events in time instead.
